heading: Low-bit quantization, which reduces weight precision, can restore forgotten information
definition: low-bit quantization of the unlearned weights restores it.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce recovery on the MUSE and TOFU benchmarks after 4-bit quantization, which reduces the precision of model weights. Recovery depends on the unlearning method and quantization setup, with conflicting MUSE results and mostly weak or absent recovery on the WMDP knowledge benchmark.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1-10B for 4-bit quantization after GA/NPO-family gradient unlearning on MUSE and TOFU. On the same Llama-2-7B MUSE setup, 2602.13151 does not reproduce it. On WMDP, RMU and NPO show no rise or a small one (2505.04416, 2407.06483, 2510.07626; NPO in 2605.15138). The exception is 2512.18035's figure-only report. 2605.15138 also finds partial NF4 recovery for SimNPO and GU+SimNPO on Qwen-3-8B WMDP-cyber. R0 at 10-100B: 2608.04519 is the only study there (counts: versions.D.studies_by_size 10-100B = 1). Its INT4 single-hop recovery rates: GA 79.7 on Qwen3-14B and 77.7 on Qwen3-32B; RMU partial at 27.6 and 17.9; PALU and AS 0.0 on Qwen3-32B. Untested for LLMs below 1B and above 100B. Vision models of unstated size are mixed: 2603.14819 partial, 2505.22310 none.
suggested_status.reason:
No catalog original tests D (counts: versions.D.original_sources_linked = []). 2410.16454 is the first report. The checker relabels its D challenges verdict (l4) as limits_scope. That verdict covers RWKU RT fill-in-the-blank 76.6→66.6, where RT had barely forgotten at full precision (target 85.9) and the authors blame utility loss. RT QA/AA rise 25.7→47.3 and 34.2→66.9. So none of the first report's D verdicts remains challenges.

Papers not flagged as sharing authors with an original reproduce 4-bit recovery on several setups:
- MUSE, LLaMA-2 7B and ICLM-7B: 2601.15538, 2606.02920, 2608.05783 (the checker finds no author overlap with 2410.16454; overlap is not checked for the other three) and 2510.00761.
- TOFU, adapter INT4 on LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-7B: 2605.02196.
- TOFU, Llama-3.2-1B: 2609.10439.
- TOFU, Gemma-2-2B: 2506.06278 (one setting, truth ratio only).
- A multi-hop benchmark on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3: 2608.04519.
2609.27355 repeats 2410.16454's values and should not count as independent.

Against:
- 2602.13151 finds no recovery on the same model, corpus and objectives.
- On WMDP, RMU does not recover in 2505.04416, 2407.06483 and 2510.07626. NPO stays flat in 2510.07626 and rises slightly on Qwen-3-8B in 2605.15138 (bio +0.037, R10; cyber +0.033, no row in the records; fractions). 2605.15138 has no RMU. Under NF4 its WMDP-bio gaps are -0.020 to +0.050. On Qwen-3-8B WMDP-cyber, however, SimNPO goes 0.270→0.403 and GU+SimNPO 0.333→0.443 (Table 2, no row in the records), about half the drop by the checker's reading. Its Table 9 gives a Qwen-family Global GA mean gap of +0.099 (no row in the records).
- Merged-model NF4 does not reproduce adapter INT4 (2605.02196).
- At 8-bit, results differ by study. No rise: 2410.16454 (NEWS) and 2605.02196's simulated adapter INT8. Partial rises: 2605.02196's merged INT8, 2609.10439 and 2603.14819. Return to the Finetuned level: 2605.12765's Llama-3.1-8B RMU forget05 (r47).

counts: versions.D.verdicts.supports.studies = 15, limits_scope.studies = 25, challenges.studies = 15. The challenges count still includes 2410.16454's l4 verdict, which the checker would relabel limits_scope.
suggested_status.open_questions:
1) Why 2602.13151 fails on the same setup. Its BF16 forget scores are higher, i.e. it forgot less before quantization. Quantizing 2410.16454's released checkpoints the way 2602.13151 does would settle it. If a clean failure replicates there, the level moves toward C.
2) Numeric WMDP recovery for GA, NPO and RMU on Zephyr-7B, since 2512.18035 is figure-only. Also whether 2605.15138's SimNPO and GU+SimNPO recovery on Qwen-3-8B WMDP-cyber appears on other models or on WMDP-bio.
3) Whether merged-model PTQ after LoRA unlearning recovers on TOFU. 2605.02196's merged NF4 does not.
4) Whether 2609.27355 shares authors or checkpoints with 2410.16454.
5) Tests above 32B, on reasoning or preference-tuned models, or on the original WHP/WMDP checkpoints.
6) Whether recovery should be measured against the quantized or the full-precision target.

original_result.result: The original paper did not test whether reducing the precision of the unlearned model's weights (quantization) recovered information.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: 4-bit quantization recovered forgotten knowledge across several unlearning methods that preserved general performance.
4-bit GPTQ restored substantial verbatim memorization after Adam-based NPO unlearning.
4-bit quantization substantially restored NPO's forgotten knowledge on MUSE Books.
INT4 quantization increased forgotten-answer truth ratios after GradDiff unlearning.
Quantization recovered forgotten WMDP knowledge, though less effectively than fine-tuning.
Simulated INT4 adapter quantization sharply increased accuracy on forgotten material after unlearning reduced it near chance.
4-bit quantization restored substantial memorization after several unlearning methods.
4-bit quantization returned GAGDR and ReLearn memorization to original-model levels.
4-bit quantization substantially restored SimNPO memorization on both MUSE corpora.
Quantization moved RMU's memorization score toward the fine-tuned model's level.
INT4 quantization restored many unlearned items across several methods.
4-bit quantization restored forgotten knowledge after KLR-regularized GA and NPO.
Quantization increased CLIP's accuracy on forgotten material after full-model unlearning updates.
4-bit quantization partially restored knowledge and memorization after GA GDR unlearning.
4-bit quantization made TULIP appear worse at forgetting, as judged by an indirect measure.
Recovery weakened with 8-bit quantization, with NPO variants, and after general performance collapsed.
Quantization did not restore knowledge after GRUN's gated unlearning.
4-bit quantization produced limited LUNAR recovery, with outputs remaining unusable.
INT4 recovery was negligible when measured by forgotten-answer probability.
INT4 quantization recovered only a small fraction of forgotten WMDP performance.
4-bit quantization increased recovery scores only in some checkpoints that retained strong general performance.
Combined quantization and translation produced only partial concept recovery in LLaVA.
INT4 quantization recovered nothing from a GA model whose general ability had collapsed.
After 4-bit quantization, recall rose by a large proportion but remained low.
INT8 quantization and SalUn showed little or partial recovery.
Quantization left memorization unchanged or reduced it for several unlearning settings.
8-bit quantization and several 4-bit methods restored memorization only partially.
NF4 quantization produced only small increases in forgotten biological knowledge.
GROM showed little or no memorization recovery after 4-bit quantization.
KUDA showed no meaningful knowledge recovery after 8-bit or 4-bit quantization.
Quantization moved NPO's memorization score only slightly toward the fine-tuned model's level.
INT4 quantization produced only partial recovery for selected TV, RMU, and PALU models.
Quantization produced only small recovery of forgotten SIN attributes.
Quantization only slightly reversed PerTA-grad unlearning.
RA2 kept forgotten WMDP performance near chance after quantization.
Quantization modestly increased NPOGDR's knowledge-test scores but sharply restored recall of exact wording.
4-bit quantization barely increased memorization in selected full-fine-tuning settings.
Layer-restricted CLIP unlearning resisted recovery through quantization.
4-bit quantization recovered nothing after plain GA caused general model performance to collapse.
Quantization recovery in OpenVLA was partial and depended on the unlearning method.
Quantization failed to restore WMDP knowledge after RMU while the model remained functional.
4-bit quantization reduced RT's fill-in-the-blank performance on RWKU.
ZO and Hybrid NPO optimizers prevented memorization recovery through 4-bit GPTQ.
Quantization did not restore accuracy on forgotten material in ResNet-18 vision classifiers.
Quantization failed to restore forgotten outputs for several LUNAR models.
4-bit and 8-bit quantization did not reverse NPO or RMU forgetting on WMDP.
INT4 quantization barely changed WMDP accuracy on forgotten material, including for RMU that preserved general performance.
4-bit quantization produced little recovery across several forgetting metrics.
Actual NF4 quantization reduced forget accuracy in merged unlearned models.
NF4 quantization produced no recovery beyond noise for several Llama and Qwen methods.
Quantization did not reverse forgetting in several NPO and RMU settings.
INT4 quantization produced negligible recovery for Qwen3-32B with PALU or AS.
Quantization barely recovered private information and sometimes improved forgetting.
4-bit RTN failed to reverse full-fine-tuning unlearning across most tested settings.
Quantization generally preserved or improved forgetting quality across several unlearning methods.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.basis: Untested lines of 2602.19275 (only KUDA models quantized), 2610.19385 (only RA2), 2502.17823 (only GRUN) and 2601.22030 (original methods not quantized as a control). LUNAR is the exception: 2605.15138, 2609.10439 and 2609.34591 quantize it.

untested.what: 2- and 3-bit quantization of utility-preserving MUSE/TOFU unlearning. Sub-4-bit is tested only on WMDP, after GA, GD and RMU on Llama3-8B.
untested.basis: The untested line of 2410.16454 says 2-bit and below were excluded, because of a large utility gap. The sub-4-bit results in pack D come from 2407.06483. Its Table 18 gives 2- and 3-bit GPTQ and AWQ after each of GA, GD and RMU on Llama3-8B, measured on WMDP, MMLU and WikiText perplexity. It has no MUSE or TOFU. Rows D01 (GA, GPTQ 2-bit), D04 (GA, AWQ 2-bit), D07 (GD, GPTQ 2-bit), D08 (GD, GPTQ 3-bit), D14 (RMU, GPTQ 3-bit) and D17 (RMU, AWQ 3-bit) are among these results, not all of them. Table 18 also has GA with GPTQ and AWQ at 3-bit, GD with AWQ at 2- and 3-bit, and RMU with GPTQ and AWQ at 2-bit.

wording_issues.issue: Recovery is reported mostly at 4-bit, and 8-bit results differ by study. At 8-bit RTN on NEWS, 2410.16454 finds none, e.g. NPO_KLR KnowMem 36.6→37.2 (r3, r5, r9, r11; the authors say 8-bit performs like full precision), and simulated adapter INT8 gives forget accuracy 0.000 in 2605.02196 (r2, r4, r6, r8). In 2605.12765 (Llama-3.1-8B, TOFU forget05; higher Mem means more forgetting), 8-bit moves at least as far as 4-bit: RMU Mem 0.15→0.03 at 4-bit NF4 and 0.01 at 8-bit LLM.int8(), the Finetuned level (r46, r47); NPO 0.54→0.49 at 4-bit and 0.44 at 8-bit (r44, r45). Partial 8-bit rises are also reported in 2609.10439 (q8 rows) and 2603.14819 (CLIP; r01, r03). At 2–3 bits, GA/GD models break and 2-bit AWQ collapses every Llama3-8B model (2407.06483 D01, D04, D07, D08), so there is nothing left to recover. The statement gives no bit width.

The result depends on how the weights were unlearned and which weights are quantized. Regularized GA/NPO, SimNPO and Adam-trained NPO recover on MUSE. These do not: RMU on WMDP (2505.04416 D1, D2; 2407.06483 D15); NPO trained with ZO or Hybrid optimizers (2510.00761 r3, r6); GROM (2608.05783 r14); KUDA (2602.19275 D4); the layer-restricted RAZOR on CLIP (2603.14819 r10). In 2605.02196, quantizing the adapter weights recovers (r1) but quantizing the merged model with NF4 does not (r17).

In most rows recovery is partial, and the reference point varies. In 2410.16454, NEWS rises to about 50 against a target of 63.9. In 2601.15538, the GA GDR baseline without QUAIL's hinge loss reaches KnowMem M2 49.54 at 4-bit, from 24.35 at 16-bit, against a target of 54.45 at 4-bit and 64.41 at 16-bit (r8). 2608.04519 restores 51–88% of items. WMDP rises are 7–16% of the gap (2505.04416). Quantization also lowers the scores of the target or base model (2602.13151 r02 verdict; 2606.02920 verdict), so the share 'restored' depends on whether it is measured against the full-precision or the quantized target. 2609.27355 r2 compares with the quantized target, 36.8.

Most recovery is measured as MUSE memorization or with TOFU proxies, and which MUSE measure recovers more depends on the method. In 2606.02920 (4-bit, MUSE News on Llama-2 7B), NPO+KLR VerbMem goes 6.32→39.35 while KnowMem goes 51.78→52.19 (R21, R22). But that KnowMem was barely forgotten (base 66.45) and ends near the base model's 4-bit value of 54.32. In the same block, GradDiff KnowMem goes 25.30→47.28 (R18) and NPO KnowMem 0.00→29.41 (R20), each a larger rise than the method's VerbMem rise (checker's reading of the same table). Accuracy on hazardous-knowledge multiple choice (WMDP) mostly does not recover (2505.04416, 2407.06483, 2510.07626), and 2605.15138's WMDP-bio cells move by −0.020 to +0.050 under NF4 (fractions; R01, R03). There are two exceptions. One is 2512.18035's figure-only report. The other is 2605.15138's Qwen-3-8B WMDP-cyber under NF4, where SimNPO goes 0.270→0.403 and GU+SimNPO 0.333→0.443 (fractions; Table 2, no row in the records).

method_sensitivity.what: 4-bit recovers where 8-bit does not in 2410.16454 (NEWS 8-bit rows r3, r5, r9, r11 vs the 4-bit rises) and in 2605.02196 (simulated INT8 0.000 in r2 vs INT4 0.262 in r1). For TULIP, the authors' own method in 2609.34591 (Llama-3.1-8B, TOFU 5%; FQ, higher = better forgetting, a proxy rather than recovered accuracy), FQ is 0.89 ± 0.13 unattacked, 0.92 ± 0.04 at 8-bit and 0.30 at 4-bit (Q45, Q47). At 2-bit, AWQ collapses every model and GA/GD models break; WMDP accuracy is then 0.24–0.25 as a fraction (2407.06483 D01, D04, D07).

method_sensitivity.factor: unlearning method, retain regularisation and how deep the full-precision forgetting is
method_sensitivity.what: Within one setup, the result changes with the method. 2606.02920, MUSE News (Llama-2 7B), 4-bit VerbMem: SimNPO 8.03→37.58 (R25) and NPO+KLR 6.32→39.35 (R21), but RMU 27.15→21.77 (R23) and GA 0.00→0.00 (R15). 2608.05783, MUSE Books (ICLM-7B), 4-bit VerbMem: SimNPO 0.00→72.5 vs GROM 2.40→2.9 (r26, r30). CLIP, CIFAR-10 forget accuracy in percent (2603.14819): SSD 52.00→62.49 vs RAZOR 52.50→53.00 at 4-bit (r02, r10). 2410.16454's verdict ties the effect to utility-preserving methods with small weight changes. 2506.12618 tests low-LR (1e-5) checkpoints because quantization is described as most effective there.

Same NPO objective, 4-bit GPTQ, VerbMem on Df. Adam: 0→48.5 (Books) and 0.9→34.0 (News). ZO: 20.7→16.2 and 21.3→17.3. Hybrid: 0→0 and 8.9→8.4 (2510.00761 r1–r6). The conflict-index groups 'iclm7b | weight_edit' and 'llama27b | weight_edit' set these rows beside 2609.27355's rises on the same model types.

method_sensitivity.factor: deployment regime: adapter-space simulation vs merged-model quantization
method_sensitivity.what: In 2605.02196, simulated INT4 on LoRA adapters raises LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct GA forget accuracy 0.028→0.262 (r1). Bitsandbytes NF4 on the merged model lowers it, 0.070→0.014 (r17). Merged bitsandbytes INT8 gives a +57% rise, 0.070→0.110 (r13).

method_sensitivity.factor: measure: verbatim vs knowledge memorization, and the choice of TOFU metric
method_sensitivity.what: Which measure rises after quantization varies, and the direction varies too. 2606.02920, MUSE News (Llama-2 7B), 4-bit: NPO+KLR VerbMem 6.32→39.35 but KnowMem 51.78→52.19 (R21, R22); SimNPO VerbMem 8.03→37.58 vs KnowMem 45.81→48.82 (R25, R26). It goes the other way for GradDiff, VerbMem 0.26→7.36 vs KnowMem 25.30→47.28 (R17, R18), and for NPO, 0.00→14.61 vs 0.00→29.41 (R19, R20). Per the check, NPO+KLR and SimNPO KnowMem had barely been forgotten at full precision (News base 66.45; base 4-bit 54.32). Gemma-2-2B GradDiff at INT4: truth ratio 0.000→0.185 but Q&A probability 0.000→0.008 (2506.06278 R26, R25). 2506.12618 (Llama-3.2-1B TOFU, 4-bit): quantization robustness Q (higher = the metric moves less) is 0.95 for Extraction Strength and 0.92 for Exact Memorization, 0.60 for Probability, and 0.48–0.61 for MIA metrics (r9, r10, r14). There, the memorization metrics move least.

RTN, AWQ and GPTQ give similar 4-bit recovery on MUSE NEWS KnowMem. GAKLR goes from 27.1 to 50.9 (bitsandbytes, defined in the text as round-to-nearest), 49.8 (AWQ) and 49.3 (GPTQ) (2609.27355 r4, r14, r16). NPO_GDR goes from 46.1 to 51.4 (4-bit RTN), 49.6 (AWQ) and 48.9 (GPTQ) (2410.16454 r10, r15, r16). No study here shows the bitsandbytes formats differing. In 2605.12765 (Llama-3.2-1B, RMU forget01; TOFU Mem, higher = more forgetting), Mem goes from 0.15 to 0.36 with NF4 and to 0.23 with LLM.int8() (r34, r35). Both move away from recovery, and NF4 is 4-bit while LLM.int8() is 8-bit, so format and bit width are confounded. RA2 on Zephyr-7B-β (2610.19385; fractions): Bio 0.2930→0.2985 (int8_bnb) and 0.2899 (nf4_bnb); Cyber 0.2730→0.2828 and 0.2929 (R1–R4). The authors say both formats stay close to the unquantized reference.

LUNAR at 4-bit on PISTOL rises slightly on Llama2-7B and Llama3-8B (r6, r7), but not on Gemma-7B or Qwen2/Qwen2.5-7B (r8–r10) (2502.07218). Multi-hop benchmark (2608.04519), INT4 single-hop recovery on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct / Qwen3-14B / Qwen3-32B, with hyperparameters tuned per method and model: GA 85.7 / 79.7 / 77.7 (R25, R31, R37), little change; AS 55.9 / 79.0 / 0.0 (R30, R36, R42); PALU 4.0 / 51.2 / 0.0 (R28, R34, R40). The same-method scale contrasts are AS and PALU, Qwen3-14B vs Qwen3-32B. TOFU Mem (higher = more forgetting), RMU forget05 (2605.12765): on Llama-3.1-8B it returns to the Finetuned level of 0.01, 0.15→0.03 at 4-bit NF4 and 0.01 at 8-bit (r46, r47). On Llama-3.2-1B it moves toward more forgetting, 0.29→0.45 at 4-bit and 0.39 at 8-bit (r38, r39, values as corrected).

method_sensitivity.factor: benchmark and split (MUSE vs WMDP subsets vs others)
method_sensitivity.what: Outcomes differ by benchmark and split, but MUSE vs WMDP does not separate them cleanly. SimNPO's verbatim memorization rises at 4-bit on MUSE (percent): News, Llama-2 7B, 8.03→37.58 (2606.02920 R25); News 2.34→38.7 and Books 0.00→72.5 (2608.05783 r10, r26). In 2605.15138 (NF4, fractions), SimNPO stays flat on WMDP-bio, 0.250 (Llama) and 0.227 (Qwen), with collapsed MMLU (R04, R11), and on MUSE (Llama 0.000→0.000, Qwen 0.001→0.013). It rises on Qwen-3-8B WMDP-cyber, 0.270→0.403 (Table 2, from the check; no pack row). In 2410.16454, RMU rises on MUSE BOOKS (ICLM-7B; KnowMem 0.0→29.3, RMU_LAT 0.0→27.4; bit width not stated; utility M4 already 0.0 at full precision) (r17, r18). It also rises on the multi-hop benchmark (2608.04519 R29), but not on WMDP (2505.04416 D1, D2; 2407.06483 D15).
